name: MET exon 14 skipping and MET amplification
summary: MET exon 14 skipping alterations are a targetable driver in NSCLC, more common in older patients and in pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma; MET amplification occurs de novo and as a key acquired resistance mechanism to EGFR and ALK TKIs.
biology: MET encodes the hepatocyte growth factor receptor. Exon 14 encodes the juxtamembrane domain containing the Y1003 binding site for the E3 ubiquitin ligase CBL. Mutations or deletions disrupting the exon 14 splice sites lead to its excision from the transcript, impairing CBL-mediated ubiquitination and receptor degradation, and causing sustained MET signalling. High-level focal MET amplification can also act as a driver, whereas polysomy and protein overexpression are less specific.
alterations: MET exon 14 skipping (splice donor/acceptor mutations, deletions, Y1003 mutations)
Focal MET amplification (de novo or acquired after EGFR/ALK TKIs)
MET protein overexpression (target for MET-directed antibody-drug conjugates in development)
Acquired MET kinase-domain mutations (D1228X, Y1230X) after type I MET inhibitors

methods: Hybrid-capture DNA NGS with intronic coverage
Fluorescence in situ hybridisation for MET amplification (MET/CEP7 ratio and gene copy number)
Immunohistochemistry for MET protein expression (not a surrogate for exon 14 skipping)
testing.specimen: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumour tissue (biopsy, resection or cytology cell block); plasma ctDNA as a complementary or initial approach
testing.notes: The diversity of exon 14 splice-site variants means DNA amplicon panels can miss alterations; RNA testing detects the skipped transcript directly. Amplification definitions vary across assays and focal high-level amplification is most predictive.

predictiveRelevance: MET exon 14 skipping predicts benefit from selective MET TKIs (capmatinib, tepotinib) and, to a lesser degree, crizotinib. High-level MET amplification acquired after EGFR TKIs is targeted with combinations of an EGFR TKI and a MET inhibitor, or with amivantamab-based strategies, mostly within trials or guided by phase II data.
resistance: On-target kinase-domain mutations (D1228X, Y1230X) affecting type I inhibitors, which may retain sensitivity to type II inhibitors
MET amplification of the mutant allele
Bypass: KRAS mutation or amplification, EGFR or HER3 activation, PI3K pathway alterations
cnsConsiderations: Capmatinib and tepotinib have reported intracranial activity in MET exon 14-altered NSCLC.
